symbols.name: W
symbols.space: a fixed finite alphabet \(\mathcal W\) with \(|\mathcal W|\ge 3\)

symbols.name: Z
symbols.space: a fixed finite alphabet \(\mathcal Z\) with \(|\mathcal Z|\ge 2\) in design A and \(|\mathcal Z|\ge 3\) in design B
symbols.role: second proxy in design A and instrument in design B

symbols.name: E
symbols.def: \(E=(X,Y)\), with the displayed labels ordered as \(11,01,10,00\).

symbols.name: p
symbols.space: the interior of the simplex on \(\mathcal E\times\mathcal W\times\mathcal Z\)
symbols.def: \(p_{ewz}=P(E=e,W=w,Z=z\mid S=1)\).

symbols.name: r
symbols.space: the interior of the simplex on \(\mathcal E\)
symbols.def: \(r_e=\sum_{w,z}p_{ewz}\).

symbols.name: T
symbols.def: \(T_e(w,z)=p_{ewz}/r_e\).

symbols.name: v
symbols.def: \(v_e(z)=\sum_w T_e(w,z)\).

symbols.name: \mathcal L
symbols.def: \(\mathcal L_e=\operatorname{aff}\{T_e(\cdot,z)/v_e(z):z\in\mathcal Z\}\) for \(e\in\mathcal E\).
symbols.role: cellwise affine line or point used by the response-cycle atlas

symbols.name: m
symbols.def: \(m_e=P(E=e)\) in the target population.
symbols.role: supplied observed population cell margins in design A and induced nuisance margins in design B

symbols.name: \Theta
symbols.space: a finite product of simplices and unit intervals
symbols.def: \(\vartheta=(\pi_i,b_i(w),g_i(z),e_i(z),s_e,c)\), where \(\pi\), every \(b_i\), and every \(g_i\) are normalized nonnegative kernels, \(e_i(z),s_e\in[0,1]\), and \(c=P_{\vartheta}(S=1)>0\).

symbols.name: P_{\vartheta}
symbols.def: The law generated by \(U\sim\pi\), \(W\mid U=i\sim b_i\), \(Z\mid U=i\sim g_i\), \(X\mid(U=i,Z=z)\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(e_i(z))\), \(Y=Y_U(X)\), and \(S\mid(E=e)\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(s_e)\).
symbols.role: law induced by a full SCM parameter

symbols.name: \mathfrak M
symbols.def: The selected four-response-type proxy model satisfying response consistency, outcome-dependent selection, proxy exclusion, and positive selected cells.

symbols.name: a
symbols.def: \(a_{ei}(z)=P_{\vartheta}(U=i,Z=z\mid E=e)\) for \(i\in\mathcal I_e\).
symbols.role: normalized latent contributions in each response cell

symbols.name: b
symbols.def: \(b_i(w)=P_{\vartheta}(W=w\mid U=i)\).

symbols.name: b^{\mathrm{bd}}
symbols.role: explicit endpoint datum for the selected assignment-boundary comparator stratum

symbols.name: a^{\mathrm{bd}}
symbols.role: explicit forced-zero assignment coefficients for the boundary comparator datum

symbols.name: T^{\mathrm{bd}}
symbols.def: \(T^{\mathrm{bd}}_e=b^{\mathrm{bd}}_i(a^{\mathrm{bd}}_{ei})^{\top}+b^{\mathrm{bd}}_j(a^{\mathrm{bd}}_{ej})^{\top}\) whenever \(\mathcal I_e=\{i,j\}\).
symbols.role: explicit positive selected cellwise proxy tables on the assignment boundary

symbols.name: r^{\mathrm{bd}}
symbols.role: selected cell margins for the boundary comparator datum

symbols.name: m^{\mathrm{bd}}
symbols.role: supplied population cell margins for the boundary comparator datum

symbols.name: s^{\mathrm{bd}}
symbols.def: In the cell order \(11,01,10,00\), \(s^{\mathrm{bd}}=(1/8,1/4,3/8,1/2)\), so \(s^{\mathrm{bd}}_em^{\mathrm{bd}}_e/(5/16)=r^{\mathrm{bd}}_e\).
symbols.role: nonconstant outcome-dependent selection law for the boundary comparator datum

symbols.name: p^{\mathrm{bd}}
symbols.def: \(p^{\mathrm{bd}}_{ewz}=r^{\mathrm{bd}}_eT^{\mathrm{bd}}_e(w,z)\).
symbols.role: explicit positive selected observable table on the assignment-boundary stratum

symbols.name: g
symbols.def: \(g(z)=P_{\vartheta}(Z=z)\) on the IV-exogenous model.

symbols.name: \pi
symbols.def: \(\pi_i=P_{\vartheta}(U=i)\).

symbols.name: \pi^{\mathrm{SK}}
symbols.def: \(\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}=(\pi_4,\pi_2,\pi_3,\pi_1)\), matching the common Kawakami (2021) and Shingaki--Kuroki (2023) response-type label order \((00,01,10,11)\).
symbols.role: response-type probabilities in the published comparator labeling

symbols.name: A^{\mathrm K}
symbols.def: For \(x\in\{0,1\}\), let \(\sigma_0=(4,2,3,1)\) and \(\sigma_1=(4,3,2,1)\), and define row \(h\) of \(A_x^{\mathrm K}(b)\) as \(\bigl(1,b_{\sigma_x(h)}(w_1),b_{\sigma_x(h)}(w_2),b_{\sigma_x(h)}(w_3)\bigr)\). This is the matrix \(A_x\) on page 12134 of Kawakami (2021), after converting its response-type order \((00,01,10,11)\) to the present labels.
symbols.role: Kawakami proxy-loading matrix used for the exact overlap and scope-separation check

symbols.name: \omega^{\mathrm K}
symbols.type: pair of conditional response-type probability vectors
symbols.def: \(\omega_x^{\mathrm K}=\bigl(P_{\vartheta}(U=4\mid X=x),P_{\vartheta}(U=2\mid X=x),P_{\vartheta}(U=3\mid X=x),P_{\vartheta}(U=1\mid X=x)\bigr)\) for \(x\in\{0,1\}\).
symbols.role: conditional response-type weights recovered by the simultaneous equations in the proof of Kawakami (2021), Theorem 1

symbols.name: \phi_{\mathrm K}
symbols.def: \(\phi_{\mathrm K}(q_0,q_1)=\bigl(q_{1,2}/(q_{1,2}+q_{1,4}),q_{0,2}/(q_{0,1}+q_{0,2})\bigr)\) whenever both denominators are positive.
symbols.role: PN/PS transformation of treatment-conditional response-type weights in Kawakami's label order

symbols.name: \mathcal K_{\mathrm K}
symbols.def: \(\mathcal K_{\mathrm K}(P_{\vartheta})\) holds when \(S=1\) almost surely and the law obeys the recursive IV-plus-proxy factorization in Figure 2(b) and equation (2) of Kawakami (2021); for each \(x\), its matrices \(A_{11,x}^{\mathrm K}\), \(A_{22,x}^{\mathrm K}\), \(A_x^{\mathrm K}(b)\), \(Q_{1,x}^{\mathrm K}\), and \(P_{1,x}^{\mathrm K}-Q_{1,x}^{\mathrm K}\) are invertible as in Theorem 1(i); the second columns of \(Q_{2,x}^{\mathrm K}(Q_{1,x}^{\mathrm K})^{-1}\) and \((P_{2,x}^{\mathrm K}-Q_{2,x}^{\mathrm K})(P_{1,x}^{\mathrm K}-Q_{1,x}^{\mathrm K})^{-1}\) differ across \(x=0,1\) as in Theorem 1(ii); and \(Y_{x,z,w}=Y_x\) and \(X_{z,w}=X_z\) as in Theorem 1(iii). Here \(P_x^{\mathrm K}\) has rows \(\bigl(1,P_{\vartheta}(Z=z_0\mid X=x)\bigr)\) and \(\bigl(P_{\vartheta}(W=w_j\mid X=x),P_{\vartheta}(W=w_j,Z=z_0\mid X=x)\bigr)\) for \(j=1,2,3\); \(Q_x^{\mathrm K}\) replaces these probabilities by their intersections with \(Y=0\); subscripts \(1,2\) select the first and last two rows; and \(A_{11,x}^{\mathrm K}\) and \(A_{22,x}^{\mathrm K}\) are the first and last \(2\times2\) diagonal blocks of \(A_x^{\mathrm K}(b)\).
symbols.role: exact no-selection overlap conditions of Kawakami (2021), Theorem 1

symbols.name: \phi_{\mathrm{SK}}
symbols.def: \(\phi_{\mathrm{SK}}(q)=\bigl(q_2/(q_2+q_4),q_2/(q_1+q_2)\bigr)\) whenever both denominators are positive.
symbols.role: PN/PS transformation of the comparator's identified response-type vector

symbols.name: \tau
symbols.def: \(\tau(\vartheta)=(\mathrm{PN}(\vartheta),\mathrm{PS}(\vartheta))=(P_{\vartheta}(U=2\mid X=1,Y=1),P_{\vartheta}(U=2\mid X=0,Y=0))\).
symbols.role: selected probabilities of necessity and sufficiency

symbols.name: \mathcal F_A
symbols.def: \(\mathcal F_A(p,m)=\{\vartheta\in\Theta:P_{\vartheta}(E,W,Z\mid S=1)=p,\ P_{\vartheta}(E)=m\}\) subject to the response, selection, and proxy conditions.
symbols.role: full two-proxy SCM fiber with supplied margins

symbols.name: \mathcal F_B
symbols.def: \(\mathcal F_B(p)=\{\vartheta\in\Theta:P_{\vartheta}(E,W,Z\mid S=1)=p,\ Z\perp U,\ Z\not\!\perp X\}\) subject to the response, selection, and proxy conditions, with \(m=P_{\vartheta}(E)\) not supplied as an observed input.
symbols.role: full relevant-IV SCM fiber with unknown margins

symbols.name: \mathcal C_A
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C_A(T)=\{(b,a):b_i\in\Delta_{\mathcal W},\ a_{ei}\in\mathbb R_{+}^{|\mathcal Z|},\ T_e=b_i a_{ei}^{\top}+b_j a_{ej}^{\top},\ a_{ei}+a_{ej}=v_e\ \text{for every }\mathcal I_e=\{i,j\}\}\).

symbols.name: q^X
symbols.def: \(q^X_z=\sum_{e:e_X=1}m_e\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_e}a_{ei}(z)\), where \(e_X\) is the treatment coordinate of cell \(e\).
symbols.role: population joint mass of \(X=1\) and \(Z=z\) in cycle coordinates

symbols.name: \mathcal C_B
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C_B(T)=\{(b,a,m,g,\pi):(b,a)\in\mathcal C_A(T),\ m\in\Delta_{\mathcal E}^{\circ},\ g\in\Delta_{\mathcal Z}^{\circ},\ \pi\in\Delta_{\{1,2,3,4\}},\ \sum_{e:i\in\mathcal I_e}m_ea_{ei}(z)=\pi_i g(z)\ \text{for all }(i,z),\ q^X_zg(z')\ne q^X_{z'}g(z)\ \text{for some }(z,z')\}\).
symbols.role: normalized relevant-IV response-cycle fiber with unknown margins and response-level shared-\(Z\) equations

symbols.name: \rho
symbols.def: \(\rho_z=g(z)/g(z_0)\) for a fixed baseline \(z_0\in\mathcal Z\).

symbols.name: D^{\mathrm{res}}
symbols.def: \(D^{\mathrm{res}}_{ei}(\rho)=(a_{ei}(z)-\rho_z a_{ei}(z_0))_{z\ne z_0}\).
symbols.role: shared-instrument residual on an incident response edge

symbols.name: \mathcal G_{\rho}
symbols.def: The four-cell graph whose links are response types with two nonzero, negatively proportional incident residual vectors \(D^{\mathrm{res}}_{ei}(\rho)\).

symbols.name: \mathcal T_A
symbols.def: \(\mathcal T_A(p,m)=\{\tau(\vartheta):\vartheta\in\mathcal F_A(p,m)\}=\{\tau_C(b,a):(b,a)\in\mathcal C_A(T)\}\).
symbols.role: identified target set in design A

symbols.name: \mathcal T_B
symbols.def: \(\mathcal T_B(p)=\{\tau(\vartheta):\vartheta\in\mathcal F_B(p)\}=\{\tau_C(b,a):(b,a,m,g,\pi)\in\mathcal C_B(T)\}\).
symbols.role: identified target set in design B

symbols.name: \Sigma
symbols.def: \(\Sigma(T)\) records every cell rank, zero support, equality or incidence of normalized column points and incident affine lines, every residual zero pattern, every signed projective transfer, and every active response-cycle product generated from \(T\).

symbols.name: n_m
symbols.def: The independent design-A margin-sample size, with \(n_m=\infty\) when \(m\) is supplied exactly.

symbols.name: \lambda
symbols.def: \(\lambda=\lim n/n_m\in(0,\infty)\) when design-A margins are estimated.

symbols.name: \zeta
symbols.def: In design B, \(\zeta=p^{-}\); in design A, \(\zeta=(p^{-},m^{-})\), where the superscript minus deletes one fixed reference cell from each simplex.
symbols.role: unconstrained coordinates for the observable law

symbols.name: \mathbb K_{\zeta}
symbols.def: The subfield of \(\mathbb R\) generated over \(\mathbb Q\) by the coordinates of the real input \(\zeta\).
symbols.role: coefficient field for exact symbolic outputs

symbols.name: \mathscr A
symbols.sig: \((T,m)\) in design A or \(T\) in design B to a finite certificate over the ordered input field
symbols.def: The desired compiler is constructed from oriented rank-two segment charts, distinct- and equal-endpoint rank-one charts, explicit inactive-row support faces, projective endpoint transfers, and residual-ratio forest propagation. For a real observable input \(\zeta\), it works over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\) and returns target agreement tests, exact target encodings, or legal target-changing lifts.
symbols.role: concrete handle for the open mixed-support classification

symbols.name: \mathfrak D
symbols.def: The union of observable rank, support, incidence, pivot, residual, cycle, and algebraic-root discriminants at which the active atlas chart or the cardinality of \(\mathcal T_A\) or \(\mathcal T_B\) can change.

symbols.name: \chi
symbols.space: the finite chart set returned by \(\mathscr A\), equipped once and for all with lexicographic order

symbols.name: \bot
symbols.def: A distinguished symbol outside the atlas chart set, returned when no certified separated rigid chart is available.

symbols.name: F_{\chi}
symbols.def: If \(\chi\ne\bot\), \(\mathscr A\) certifies \(\chi\) as a rigid chart at \(z\), and its rational expression or selected simple real-algebraic root is evaluable, then \(F_{\chi}(z)\) is that exact value using its twice continuously differentiable local continuation. In every other case, including \(\chi=\bot\) or a nonrigid chart, set \(F_{\chi}(z)=(0,0)\).
symbols.role: total chartwise PN/PS evaluation with explicit fallback

symbols.name: J_{\chi}
symbols.def: On a certified rigid local continuation, \(J_{\chi}(z)=\partial F_{\chi}(z)/\partial z^{\top}\), using implicit differentiation on a simple algebraic-root chart; in every fallback case set \(J_{\chi}(z)=0\).
symbols.role: total chartwise target derivative with zero fallback

symbols.name: d_{\chi}
symbols.def: \(d_{\chi}(z)=\inf\{\|z-u\|_2:u\text{ lies in the closure of the observable domain of chart }\chi\}\).

symbols.name: \eta
symbols.def: \(\eta_{\chi}(\zeta)\) is the minimum absolute normalized slack over the finitely many strict inequalities, nonzero pivots, denominators, line separations, and simple-root derivatives used by chart \(\chi\), evaluated through its continuous local extension.

symbols.name: \widehat p_n
symbols.def: The empirical multinomial table from \(n\) independent selected observations of \((E,W,Z)\).

symbols.name: \widehat\pi_n^{\mathrm{SK}}
symbols.def: The response-type probability vector obtained by applying equations (8)--(11) of Shingaki--Kuroki (2023) to the empirical no-selection table \(\widehat p_n\), in their label order \((00,01,10,11)\).
symbols.role: published experimental-proxy plug-in estimator used in the comparator reduction

symbols.name: \widehat m_n
symbols.def: The empirical margin vector from an independent multinomial sample of size \(n_m\) when design-A margins are estimated; set \(\widehat m_n=m\) when they are supplied exactly.

symbols.name: \widehat\zeta_n
symbols.def: The reduced-coordinate vector formed from \(\widehat p_n\) and, in design A, \(\widehat m_n\).

symbols.name: \Omega_{\zeta}
symbols.def: For design B, \(\Omega_{\zeta}=\operatorname{diag}(p^{-})-p^{-}p^{-\top}\). For design A with estimated margins, append the independent block \(\lambda\{\operatorname{diag}(m^{-})-m^{-}m^{-\top}\}\); omit that block for known margins.
symbols.role: asymptotic covariance of the reduced observable coordinates

symbols.name: \widehat\Omega_n
symbols.def: Replace \(p^{-}\), \(m^{-}\), and \(\lambda\) in \(\Omega_{\zeta}\) by \(\widehat p_n^{-}\), \(\widehat m_n^{-}\), and \(n/n_m\), respectively; omit the margin block when margins are known.

symbols.name: \widehat\chi_n
symbols.type: atlas chart label or fallback label
symbols.def: Among labels that \(\mathscr A\) certifies as rigid charts and that satisfy \(d_{\chi}(\widehat\zeta_n)\le t_n\) and \(\eta_{\chi}(\widehat\zeta_n)\ge\varepsilon/2\), choose the lexicographically first; if this set is empty, set \(\widehat\chi_n=\bot\).

symbols.name: \widehat\gamma_n
symbols.def: \(\widehat\gamma_n=1\) exactly when \(\widehat\chi_n\ne\bot\) and the raw sandwich matrix \(J_{\widehat\chi_n}(\widehat\zeta_n)\widehat\Omega_nJ_{\widehat\chi_n}(\widehat\zeta_n)^{\top}\) is positive definite; otherwise \(\widehat\gamma_n=0\).

symbols.name: \widehat\tau_n
symbols.def: \(\widehat\tau_n=F_{\widehat\chi_n}(\widehat\zeta_n)\), so \(\widehat\tau_n=(0,0)\) when \(\widehat\chi_n=\bot\).
symbols.role: total deterministically selected chartwise plug-in estimator

symbols.name: V_{\tau}
symbols.def: \(V_{\tau}=J_{\chi}(\zeta)\Omega_{\zeta}J_{\chi}(\zeta)^{\top}\) on any incident first-order-compatible chart.

symbols.name: \widehat V_n
symbols.def: If \(\widehat\gamma_n=1\), set \(\widehat V_n=J_{\widehat\chi_n}(\widehat\zeta_n)\widehat\Omega_nJ_{\widehat\chi_n}(\widehat\zeta_n)^{\top}\); if \(\widehat\gamma_n=0\), set \(\widehat V_n=I_2\).
symbols.role: total plug-in covariance estimator with identity fallback

symbols.name: \mathfrak R_{\varepsilon}
symbols.def: The rigid laws having a nonempty collection of incident atlas charts with \(\eta_{\chi}(\zeta)\ge\varepsilon\), identical target value and Jacobian across all such incident charts, distance at least \(\varepsilon\) from every incompatible chart closure, twice continuously differentiable chart extensions, and \(\lambda_{\min}(V_{\tau})\ge\varepsilon\).

symbols.name: W_n
symbols.def: If \(\widehat\gamma_n=1\), set \(W_n=\{t:n(t-\widehat\tau_n)^{\top}\widehat V_n^{-1}(t-\widehat\tau_n)\le\chi^2_{2,1-\alpha}\}\cap[0,1]^2\); if \(\widehat\gamma_n=0\), set \(W_n=[0,1]^2\).

symbols.name: C_n
symbols.def: Intersect the relevant probability simplices with simultaneous two-sided Clopper--Pearson intervals for every selected-table cell and every independently estimated margin cell, allocating total tail error \(\beta_n\) by Bonferroni across all intervals and the two samples.

symbols.name: \ell_n
symbols.def: The sum of the selected-table multinomial log-likelihood and, when margins are estimated, the independent margin multinomial log-likelihood.

symbols.name: \Delta_n
symbols.def: For \(t\in[0,1]^2\), \(\Delta_n(t)=2\{\ell_n(\widehat\zeta_n)-\sup_{q:\,t\in\mathcal T(q)}\ell_n(q)\}\), with \(\mathcal T=\mathcal T_A\) in design A and \(\mathcal T=\mathcal T_B\) in design B; \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{rep}}(t)\) is the same statistic recomputed on an independent multinomial replicate under \(q\).
symbols.role: likelihood discrepancy for a candidate PN/PS value

symbols.name: \operatorname{pv}_n
symbols.def: The Berger--Boos calibrated tail probability in the definition of \(K_n\), using the exact multinomial law, preliminary region \(C_n\), and additive budget \(\beta_n\).

symbols.name: K_n
symbols.def: \(K_n=\{t\in[0,1]^2:\operatorname{pv}_n(t)>\alpha\}\), where \(\operatorname{pv}_n(t)=\min\{1,\beta_n+\sup_{q\in C_n:\,t\in\mathcal T(q)}P_q[\Delta_n^{\mathrm{rep}}(t)\ge\Delta_n^{\mathrm{obs}}(t)]\}\); here \(\mathcal T=\mathcal T_A\) or \(\mathcal T_B\), and the supremum over an empty set is zero.
symbols.role: Berger--Boos calibrated confidence-fiber inversion for PN/PS

symbols.name: d_{\mathrm H}
symbols.def: \(d_{\mathrm H}(A,B)=\max\{\sup_{a\in A}\inf_{b\in B}\|a-b\|_2,\sup_{b\in B}\inf_{a\in A}\|a-b\|_2\}\).

symbols.name: s^{\mathrm G}
symbols.role: selection probabilities imposed in the GEUVADIS analysis

symbols.name: p^{\mathrm G}
symbols.def: The selected contingency table formed from the released GEUVADIS gene-set number 50 data with \(X\) equal to binarized SWAP70 expression, \(Y\) equal to binarized SBF2-AS1 expression, \(Z\) equal to rs7124238 allele count, and \(W\) equal to the three coarse population groups.

symbols.name: m^{\mathrm G}
symbols.def: \(m^{\mathrm G}_e=(r^{\mathrm G}_e/s^{\mathrm G}_e)/\sum_f(r^{\mathrm G}_f/s^{\mathrm G}_f)\), where \(r^{\mathrm G}_e=\sum_{w,z}p^{\mathrm G}_{ewz}\).
symbols.role: population cell margins implied by the imposed GEUVADIS selection law

assumptions.condition: \(Y=Y_U(X)\) almost surely, with the four response maps encoded by \(U\).
\(\widehat p_n\) is formed from \(n\) independent draws from \(p\); when design-A margins are estimated, \(\widehat m_n\) is formed from an independent multinomial sample of size \(n_m\).

definitions.name: Selected four-response-type proxy model
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M=\{P_{\vartheta}:\vartheta\in\Theta,\ Y=Y_U(X),\ S\perp(U,W,Z)\mid(X,Y),\ W\perp(X,Y,Z,S)\mid U,\ p_{ewz}>0\}\).

definitions.name: Design-B full fiber
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal F_B(p)=\{\vartheta\in\Theta:P_{\vartheta}\in\mathfrak M,\ P_{\vartheta}(E,W,Z\mid S=1)=p,\ Z\perp U,\ Z\not\!\perp X\}\).

definitions.name: Normalized response-cycle fibers
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal C_A(T)\) and \(\mathcal C_B(T)\) are the explicit nonnegative factorization sets in the symbol table, with \(\mathcal C_B\) adding induced unknown margins, their compatibility-implied positivity, a common \(Z\) law, response-level shared-\(Z\) equations, and relevance.

definitions.name: PN/PS rigidity
definitions.construction: Design A is rigid at \((p,m)\) when \(|\mathcal T_A(p,m)|=1\); design B is rigid at \(p\) when \(|\mathcal T_B(p)|=1\).

definitions.name: Mixed-support atlas handle
definitions.construction: Construct \(\mathscr A\) by enumerating labeled support faces; use oriented segment boxes on rank-two cells, projective endpoint transfers on distinct-endpoint rank-one cells, bounded split vectors on equal-endpoint cells, and the residual-ratio forest on design-B charts; glue component target values and lift any disagreement to full SCMs. All symbolic arithmetic is over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).

definitions.name: Legal target-changing certificate
definitions.construction: A certificate is \((\vartheta_0,\vartheta_1)\in\mathcal F_A(p,m)^2\) or \((\vartheta_0,\vartheta_1)\in\mathcal F_B(p)^2\) such that \(\tau(\vartheta_0)\ne\tau(\vartheta_1)\); both points must be interior only when the certified nonrigid stratum is interior.

definitions.name: First-order separated rigid stratum
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak R_{\varepsilon}\) is the set of rigid observable coordinates \(\zeta\) for which the incident-chart set \(\Gamma(\zeta)=\{\chi:d_{\chi}(\zeta)=0,\ \eta_{\chi}(\zeta)\ge\varepsilon\}\) is nonempty; every pair in \(\Gamma(\zeta)\) has the same \(F_{\chi}(\zeta)\) and \(J_{\chi}(\zeta)\); every incompatible chart closure is at Euclidean distance at least \(\varepsilon\); each incident \(F_{\chi}\) has a twice continuously differentiable extension on an \(\varepsilon\)-neighborhood; and \(\lambda_{\min}(V_{\tau})\ge\varepsilon\).

definitions.name: Deterministically selected chartwise Wald procedure
definitions.construction: Set \(t_n=n^{-1/4}\) and compute the lexicographic certified-rigid selector \(\widehat\chi_n\), using \(\bot\) if no chart qualifies. Set \(\widehat\tau_n=F_{\widehat\chi_n}(\widehat\zeta_n)\). If \(\widehat\gamma_n=1\), report the sandwich covariance and its Wald ellipse; if \(\widehat\gamma_n=0\), set \(\widehat V_n=I_2\) and report \(W_n=[0,1]^2\).

definitions.name: Calibrated transition-robust confidence fiber
definitions.construction: Build \(C_n\) from Bonferroni-calibrated two-sided Clopper--Pearson cell intervals with total error \(\beta_n=\min\{n^{-2},\alpha/2\}\). For each \(t\in[0,1]^2\), compute the profile deviance \(\Delta_n(t)\), take the supremum of its exact replicate tail probability over \(q\in C_n\) satisfying \(t\in\mathcal T(q)\), add \(\beta_n\), truncate at one, and set \(K_n=\{t:\operatorname{pv}_n(t)>\alpha\}\).

definitions.name: GEUVADIS certification handle
definitions.construction: Reconstruct \(p^{\mathrm G}\) from the released counts, derive \(m^{\mathrm G}\) from the imposed \(s^{\mathrm G}\), impose the response-level shared-\(Z\) and relevance equations, run \(\mathscr A\), and apply the calibrated profile confidence-fiber procedure \(K_n\).

statements.statement: For every \(\vartheta\in\mathcal F_A(p,m)\) or \(\vartheta\in\mathcal F_B(p)\), positivity of the selected table and \(c=P_{\vartheta}(S=1)>0\) imply \(P_{\vartheta}(E=e,S=1)=c r_e>0\) and therefore \(m_e=P_{\vartheta}(E=e)\ge c r_e>0\) for every \(e\in\mathcal E\). Consequently, a nonempty design-A fiber forces the supplied observed margin vector \(m\) to lie in \(\Delta_{\mathcal E}^{\circ}\), and every compatible design-B SCM induces positive population margins.
statements.justification: Population-margin positivity is a compatibility implication of observed positivity and positive selection mass, not an independent maintained condition.
statements.gap: The anchor imposes positive quantities in its regular formulas but does not isolate this elementary full-fiber compatibility consequence.
statements.consumer: The cycle lift and residual-forest theorem may use positive margin ratios without strengthening either design's assumptions.

statements.statement: For every positive selected table \(p\) and supplied margin vector \(m\) with \(\mathcal F_A(p,m)\ne\varnothing\), the map \(\vartheta\mapsto(b,a)\) sends \(\mathcal F_A(p,m)\) onto \(\mathcal C_A(T)\) and preserves \(\tau=\tau_C\). For design B it sends \(\mathcal F_B(p)\) onto \(\mathcal C_B(T)\) and preserves \(\tau=\tau_C\). Conversely, every point of either cycle fiber has a legal full finite SCM lift, including zero response masses and boundary proxy or assignment mechanisms.
statements.justification: This equivalence makes every algebraic certificate causally legal and prevents factorization-only counterexamples.
statements.gap: The anchor proves recovery under regular inversions but does not state an onto nonnegative lift covering zero latent masses and unknown-margin IV fibers.
statements.consumer: Every rigidity formula and nonrigidity twin returned by the atlas is translated into a full selected SCM.

statements.statement: If every \(T_e\) has rank two, \(\mathcal C_A(T)\) is exactly the union of at most \(2^4\) products of closed rational endpoint intervals obtained by orienting each observed segment. On each nonempty product, \(\tau_C\) is constant if and only if the endpoint intervals for response types \(1,2,4\) are singletons. Global rigidity holds if and only if those constants agree across all products; otherwise rational endpoint choices yield a legal target-changing certificate.
statements.justification: This is the complete boundary result on the largest regular-rank branch and exhibits target rigidity without factor uniqueness.
statements.gap: Rank-two segment geometry is standard, but no prior result glues four labeled cells and characterizes only PN/PS constancy across orientation components.
statements.consumer: It certifies assignment-boundary PN/PS values on singular support faces.

statements.statement: Fix \((b,a)\in\mathcal C_A(T)\) and write \(\rho_z=g(z)/g(z_0)>0\). For every response type \(i\) and its incident cells \(e,f\), define \(D_{ei}(\rho)=(a_{ei}(z)-\rho_z a_{ei}(z_0))_{z\ne z_0}\). Positive unknown margins satisfying the response-level shared-\(Z\) equations exist if and only if, at each \(i\), both residuals vanish or they are nonzero and negatively proportional; the nonzero links determine positive margin ratios, whose product equals one on every active cycle, while each forest component retains one positive scale subject to normalization. Adding \(q^X_zg(z')\ne q^X_{z'}g(z)\) for some \((z,z')\) is necessary and sufficient for membership in \(\mathcal C_B(T)\).
statements.justification: The theorem removes unknown margins as an opaque bilinear block and isolates the only cycle obstruction.
statements.gap: The anchor's population independence equation does not characterize response-level IV exogeneity on inactive and boundary branches.
statements.consumer: The structural compiler can decide relevant-IV compatibility and preserve IV restrictions when extracting twins.

statements.statement: Can the mixed-support atlas handle \(\mathscr A\) be completed so that, for every fixed finite \((\mathcal W,\mathcal Z)\) and every nonempty \(\mathcal C_A(T)\) or \(\mathcal C_B(T)\), it enumerates all labeled rank-one and rank-two incidence charts, inactive rows, coincident endpoints, residual forests, real algebraic components, and support faces; decides whether \(\tau_C\) agrees within and across them; and returns either an exact target value or a legal target-changing certificate, without using a generic two-copy quantifier-elimination predicate as the classification?
statements.justification: This exhaustion and gluing problem is the single load-bearing open mathematical step.
statements.gap: Neither causal proxy identification nor NMF rigidity literature supplies a global target-image classification across all boundary components of this labeled cycle.
statements.consumer: Solving it turns sufficient regular identification into a complete decision rule for every legal finite anchor-model observable law.

statements.statement: For design A, \(|\mathcal T_A(p,m)|=1\) if and only if the finite observable rank/support/cycle conditions returned by \(\mathscr A(T,m)\) hold. For design B, \(|\mathcal T_B(p)|=1\) if and only if the corresponding residual-forest and cycle conditions returned by \(\mathscr A(T)\) hold. For an arbitrary real input \(\zeta\), every rigid output is either a rational expression in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\) or a uniquely ordered real element of a finite algebraic extension, certified by a square-free polynomial in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}[q]\) and Thom sign data. If \(\zeta\) is explicitly rational, this certificate may instead be normalized to a square-free integer polynomial and rational isolating interval. Every nonrigid output contains two legal full SCMs with identical observables and supplied margins, when supplied, but different \(\tau\); both SCMs are strictly positive whenever the nonrigid stratum is interior.
statements.justification: This is the necessary-and-sufficient theorem-level kernel and gives an exact coefficient-field meaning to every atlas output.
statements.gap: Published proxy results give sufficient full-rank formulas, while published factorization results target nuisance uniqueness rather than PN/PS constancy.
statements.consumer: Analysts receive a definitive identification certificate or an explicit observational-equivalence refutation for any fixed finite selected table.

statements.statement: On every observable law satisfying Conditions 2--3 of Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki (2026), the rigid value returned by \(\mathscr A\) equals the PN/PS value obtained from their Appendix equations (A.28)--(A.33). The same atlas is defined on additional singular and boundary observable laws not covered by those regular conditions, including design-A support-face strata with rank loss, coincident endpoints, inactive rows, or forced-zero incident coefficients and analogous design-B strata governed by response-level shared-\(Z\) residual forests. On each such law, the full-rigidity theorem returns either a target-rigidity certificate with an exact value or a legal target-changing full-SCM certificate.
statements.justification: This supporting result validates agreement with the anchor formulas on their regular domain and records the singular and boundary domains handled by the atlas.
statements.gap: The 2026 anchor supplies regular inversion formulas but does not state a full-fiber decision procedure on singular support faces or residual-forest boundary strata.
statements.consumer: Users of the anchor formulas can verify numerical agreement on regular tables and obtain a defined certification workflow when regular inversions are unavailable.

On the local no-selection experimental submodel \(S=1\) almost surely and \(X\perp(U,W,Z)\), impose \(W\perp Z\mid U\) and Conditions (1)--(3) of Theorem 1 of Shingaki--Kuroki (2023). After the label conversion \(\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}=(\pi_4,\pi_2,\pi_3,\pi_1)\), \(\mathcal T_A(p,r)=\{\phi_{\mathrm{SK}}(\pi^{\mathrm{SK}})\}\), the exact value returned by \(\mathscr A\) equals this singleton, and \(\phi_{\mathrm{SK}}(\widehat\pi_n^{\mathrm{SK}})\xrightarrow{P}\phi_{\mathrm{SK}}(\pi^{\mathrm{SK}})\). As a separate boundary-coverage check, for \(|\mathcal W|=|\mathcal Z|=3\), the explicit datum \((b^{\mathrm{bd}},a^{\mathrm{bd}},T^{\mathrm{bd}},r^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}},s^{\mathrm{bd}},p^{\mathrm{bd}})\) has \(\mathcal F_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})

The relative-open support-face chart that preserves these four zero positions, positivity of every other displayed incident coefficient and every proxy endpoint, the strict order of \(b_1^{\mathrm{bd}},b_2^{\mathrm{bd}},b_4^{\mathrm{bd}}\) on their common line, transversality of the two remaining incident lines, and \(m

statements.justification: This supporting theorem validates the atlas on the exact experimental overlap and on a fully specified selected assignment-boundary datum.
statements.gap: Shingaki--Kuroki (2023), Theorem 1 and equations (8)--(11), identify and estimate the full response-type vector under no selection, randomized treatment, invertible cell matrices, and determinant-ratio separation; the cited theorem does not address selected forced-zero cycle fibers.
statements.consumer: Experimental users can check agreement with the published plug-in estimand, while selected-data users can verify the separate boundary certificate under the present model.

statements.statement: For every \(\vartheta\in\mathcal F_B(p)\) in the no-selection overlap satisfying \(\mathcal K_{\mathrm K}(P_{\vartheta})\), the simultaneous equations in the proof of Kawakami (2021), Theorem 1 on pages 12135--12137 identify \(\omega_0^{\mathrm K}\) and \(\omega_1^{\mathrm K}\). If \(\mathcal T_B(p)\) is a singleton, its atlas value agrees with \(\tau(\vartheta)=\phi_{\mathrm K}(\omega_0^{\mathrm K},\omega_1^{\mathrm K})\). Kawakami's identified scope is the four joint probabilities of binary potential-outcome types, together with their treatment-conditional weights used for PN and PS, under Figure 2(b), equation (2), and Theorem 1(i)--(iii). For the single explicit selected boundary datum \((p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})\), \(\mathcal F_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathcal T_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})=\{(1/2,1/2)\}\), but \(A_x^{\mathrm K}(b^{\mathrm{bd}})\) is singular for each \(x\): because \(\mathcal W=\{w_1,w_2,w_3\}\), its first column is the sum of its last three columns. Thus this legal selected response-cycle law violates the named invertibility assumption in Kawakami's Theorem 1(i) while remaining classified by the atlas; this is a strict scope separation, not a subsumption claim.
statements.justification: This supporting theorem records the exact no-selection IV-plus-proxy overlap and a one-law separation from Kawakami's regular invertibility domain.
statements.gap: Kawakami (2021), Figure 2(b), equation (2), Theorem 1(i)--(iii), and its appendix identify all four response-type probabilities under invertible proxy-loading and observable blocks plus cross-treatment separation, but do not classify selected or singular response-cycle fibers.
statements.consumer: IV-plus-proxy analysts can audit agreement on Kawakami-regular laws and recognize a concrete selected boundary law for which the regular matrix method is unavailable but the atlas still returns an exact certificate.

statements.statement: For fixed \(k=|\mathcal Z|\) and \(\ell=|\mathcal W|\), the finite structural chart enumeration of \(\mathscr A\) terminates using arithmetic and order tests over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\). There is an explicit computable constant \(B_{k,\ell}\le 2^{2^{C(k\ell+k+\ell)}}\), for a universal constant \(C\), bounding the number of labeled charts and the algebraic degree over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\). If every coordinate of \(\zeta\) is an explicitly encoded rational whose numerator and denominator have binary length at most \(L\), a Turing implementation terminates; after clearing denominators, every algebraic target certificate uses a square-free integer polynomial of degree at most \(B_{k,\ell}\) and rational isolating endpoints, and every coefficient and endpoint has bit length at most \(B_{k,\ell}(L+1)^C\). The classification is obtained from the structural charts in \(\mathscr A\), not by reporting generic two-copy quantifier elimination.
statements.justification: The field-relative statement separates symbolic exactness for real data from bit complexity for rational encodings.
statements.gap: Fixed-dimensional real algebraic decision is known, but no end-to-end field-relative certificate and rational-input size bound exists for this structural response-cycle compiler.
statements.consumer: Symbolic implementations can certify real-parameter outputs, while exact-arithmetic implementations can validate rational-data certificates with explicit size bounds.

statements.statement: Uniformly over compact subsets of \(\mathfrak R_{\varepsilon}\), under independent multinomial sampling and \(n/n_m\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)\) when margins are estimated, the deterministic selector \(\widehat\chi_n\) chooses an incident first-order-compatible rigid chart and \(\widehat\gamma_n=1\) with probability tending to one. On these certified separated rigid charts, \(\widehat\Omega_n\xrightarrow{P}\Omega_{\zeta}\), \(\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_n-\tau)\Rightarrow N(0,V_{\tau})\), and \(\widehat V_n\xrightarrow{P}V_{\tau}\). Because \(\lambda_{\min}(V_{\tau})\ge\varepsilon\), scalar contrasts and the elliptical branch of \(W_n\) have asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\). If no chart is certified, the total procedure returns \(\widehat\chi_n=\bot\), \(\widehat\tau_n=(0,0)\), \(\widehat V_n=I_2\), and \(W_n=[0,1]^2\), with no covariance-consistency or Wald-coverage assertion for that fallback branch.
statements.justification: The chart rule, covariance formula, and nonsingularity margin make regular-stratum Wald inference operational and falsifiable.
statements.gap: The anchor and earlier response-type estimators establish regular-case normality only for their inverse formulas, not for deterministically selected rational and simple algebraic rigid charts.
statements.consumer: Separated empirical tables obtain reproducible standard errors and Wald regions on every first-order-compatible atlas chart.

statements.statement: For the Clopper--Pearson preliminary region \(C_n\), profile discrepancy \(\Delta_n\), and Berger--Boos calibration in \(\operatorname{pv}_n\), \(P_{\vartheta}\{\tau(\vartheta)\in K_n\}\ge 1-\alpha\) at every sample size for every \(\vartheta\) in either design. The bound holds along arbitrary sequences approaching \(\mathfrak D\), including point-to-set transitions. Uniformly over compact subsets of \(\mathfrak R_{\varepsilon}\), \(\sqrt n\,d_{\mathrm H}(K_n,W_n)\xrightarrow{P}0\); equivalently, the local profile boundary and the Wald ellipse have the same first-order quadratic expansion and \(\chi^2_{2,1-\alpha}\) calibration. At any law with a non-singleton identified set or without the separated-chart conditions, the theorem asserts coverage only and makes no claim that \(\operatorname{diam}(K_n)\) shrinks.
statements.justification: Exact nuisance calibration preserves coverage at transitions, while the explicit Hausdorff comparison recovers ordinary Wald geometry on separated charts.
statements.gap: Existing weak-identification and stable-bound procedures do not calibrate a profile discrepancy over this changing selected-SCM fiber or establish its first-order agreement with chart-specific Wald inference.
statements.consumer: Boundary-sensitive PN/PS analyses receive honest uncertainty without interpreting a nonshrinking confidence fiber as point identification.

statements.statement: Implementation corollary (definitional normalization). If every selection probability \(s_e=P_{\vartheta}(S=1\mid E=e)\) is known and positive, then the population margin is identified by \(m_e=(r_e/s_e)/\sum_{f\in\mathcal E}(r_f/s_f)\). The IV-plus-proxy implementation with known selection therefore intersects \(\mathcal C_B(T)\) with this normalized value of \(m\).
statements.justification: This is a definitional reweighting used to instantiate the application fiber, not a claimed research contribution.
statements.gap: The identity is elementary normalization of observed selected-cell margins by known selection probabilities.
statements.consumer: The GEUVADIS implementation uses the population margins implied by its imposed selection scheme.

statements.statement: Validation corollary (published Tian--Pearl sanity check). Suppose locally that \(S=1\) almost surely, \(X\perp U\) under \(P_{\vartheta}\), and \(P_{\vartheta}(U=3)=0\). Then the atlas value reduces to the Tian--Pearl formulas \(\mathrm{PN}=\{P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)-P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=0)\}/P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)\) and \(\mathrm{PS}=\{P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)-P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=0)\}/P_{\vartheta}(Y=0\mid X=0)\). These three hypotheses are local to this validation corollary and are not conditions on either main design.
statements.justification: This is a validation reduction to the published classical formulas, not a claimed research contribution.
statements.gap: Tian and Pearl (2000) already establish the benchmark; the only role here is to verify that the atlas preserves it.
statements.consumer: Implementers can use the classical formulas as a regression test for the generalized certificates.

statements.statement: For \((p^{\mathrm G},s^{\mathrm G})\), does the induced known-margin relevant-IV fiber pass exact compatibility and relevance, and is \(\tau\) rigid on that fiber? Using the GEUVADIS audit handle, return either the exact atlas stratum and PN/PS formula with transition-robust uncertainty, or two legal full SCMs with identical \((p^{\mathrm G},m^{\mathrm G})\) and different targets; report model incompatibility separately from nonidentification.
statements.justification: The public case study is a high-value falsification target because its bootstrap estimates reach both logical boundaries.
statements.gap: The published application assumes the graph and regular conditions but does not certify compatibility, rank/support stratum, or transition-robust coverage.
statements.consumer: Researchers interpreting SWAP70-to-SBF2-AS1 attribution receive either a defensible causal number or an explicit nonidentification certificate.

sampling_model.design: Independent multinomial sampling from the selected law \(p=P(E,W,Z\mid S=1)\), with an independent margin multinomial sample in design A when margins are estimated and \(n/n_m\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)\).
sampling_model.units: Each unit contributes one draw of \((E,W,Z)\) conditional on \(S=1\); the finite SCM is a superpopulation model.
sampling_model.treatment: \(X\) is binary and may be confounded with the response type; in design B its assignment probability may depend on \((U,Z)\).
sampling_model.overlap: All selected cells are positive. Supplied design-A margins remain observed inputs, but their positivity is forced whenever the full fiber is nonempty because \(P(E=e)\ge P(E=e,S=1)=c r_e>0\). Wald inference is restricted to first-order-compatible charts with \(\eta_{\chi}\ge\varepsilon\), twice continuously differentiable chart extensions, positive distance from incompatible chart closures, and \(\lambda_{\min}(V_{\tau})\ge\varepsilon\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Reduced multinomial coordinates use empirical frequencies and the explicit block-diagonal estimator \(\widehat\Omega_n\). The deterministic \(n^{-1/4}\) rule selects the first certified separated rigid chart; if none exists, the estimator uses its declared numerical fallback and the reported region is \([0,1]^2\). Transition inference uses a profile multinomial deviance, a \(1-\beta_n\) Clopper--Pearson preliminary region, and Berger--Boos exact nuisance calibration.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 and Corollary 1 identify PN and PS under positive observed tables, invertible proxy matrices, and unequal determinant-ratio conditions.
Formula (5) identifies a causal effect under a proxy rank condition without identifying the measurement mechanism.
Proposition 3.3 characterizes infinitesimal rigidity of an exact nonnegative factorization by its admissible-motion cone.
Theorems 5--9 give necessary support conditions and sufficient sequential recovery conditions for selected NMF factors.
Theorem 1 gives sufficient positive-scattering thresholds for minimality and uniqueness of nonnegative tensor decompositions.
Theorem 3.4 gives a regular root-n estimator for a linear proximal target without uniqueness of the bridge solution.

Theorem 1 identifies all four response-type probabilities in a randomized experiment under positive conditional tables, \(W\perp Z\mid U\), \(X\perp(U,Z,W)\), invertible cell matrices, and unequal determinant ratios; equations (8)--(11) give plug-in estimators.

Theorem 1 identifies all four joint probabilities of binary potential-outcome types under Figure 2(b)'s IV-plus-proxy recursive factorization, the five invertibility requirements in condition (i), the cross-treatment second-column separation in condition (ii), and the two exclusion restrictions in condition (iii).

Theorems 2--5 give sound closed-form bounds for a representative family of discrete probabilities of causation from standard experimental and observational distributions, while general-dimensional tightness remains open in the current version.
Conditional quasi-likelihood-ratio tests have uniformly correct asymptotic size without strong identification.
E-variable inversion yields exact anytime-valid confidence sets for contingency-table parameters.
Theorem 4 identifies PN and PS under exogeneity and monotonicity, and equations (15)--(18) give sharp bounds otherwise.

tldr: For every labeled finite four-response-type model with outcome-dependent selection and proxy-cycle restrictions, the field-level kernel is a boundary-complete response-cycle atlas for PN/PS target rigidity. A structural compiler stratifies the full nonnegative fiber by observable ranks, supports, endpoint incidences, and cycle products; it treats supplied-margin two-proxy data and unknown-margin relevant-IV data through response-level shared-\(Z\) residual forests. The main theorem gives necessary and sufficient target-constancy conditions, exact coefficient-field values on rigid strata, and legal same-observable SCM twins on nonrigid strata. Supporting results verify agreement with published regular proxy formulas on their stated domains, including Kawakami's no-selection IV-plus-proxy theorem, and exhibit an explicit selected boundary law whose proxy-loading matrix violates Kawakami's invertibility condition while the atlas remains decisive. Positivity of compatible population margins follows from positive selected cells and \(c=P(S=1)>0\). Integer-polynomial certificates, isolating intervals, and bit bounds are reserved for explicitly rational tables. A total chart procedure uses a conservative full-square fallback when no separated rigid chart is certified; Wald inference is asserted only on certified separated charts, while calibrated confidence-fiber inversion remains honest at identification transitions.

project_justification.gap: Published no-selection and selected-proxy formulas identify response-type targets under regular matrix invertibility and separation, including Kawakami's IV-plus-proxy conditions, but they do not decide PN/PS constancy when ranks fall, assignment coefficients reach nonnegative faces, endpoints coincide, selection changes population margins, or shared-instrument equations couple unknown margins. General discrete-PoC compatible-model bounds do not impose the selected proxy factorizations or label their cycle components.
project_justification.niche: The four response types form a labeled cycle on which a two-dimensional causal target can be rigid even when the full factorization moves. Its selected proxy-cycle fiber is generally nonpolyhedral and differs from both Kawakami's regular no-selection IV-plus-proxy system and the compatible-model polytope used for unrestricted PoC bounds. The field-level problem is a global target-image classification across ranks, supports, real components, and induced-margin equations.
project_justification.fill: The response-cycle atlas gives necessary and sufficient target-constancy conditions over the selected four-type SCM class, returns coefficient-field targets or legal countermodels on every component and face, and handles both supplied-margin two-proxy and unknown-margin relevant-IV designs. Supporting overlap checks recover the published regular formulas; a separate explicit-law certificate records scope beyond Kawakami's invertibility domain without asserting subsumption or extension. Deterministic separated-chart Wald inference and exactly calibrated confidence-fiber inversion complete the statistical layer.

related_work: Shingaki, Yoshida, and Kuroki (2026), Theorem 1, Corollary 1, and Appendix equations (A.23)--(A.33), provide the selected four-response-type causal model and regular inversion formulas. The supporting anchor-agreement theorem verifies that the atlas returns the same PN/PS values under those conditions and records singular and boundary observable laws on which the atlas instead uses support-face or residual-forest certificates. Shingaki and Kuroki (2023), Theorem 1 and equations (8)--(11), identify and estimate all four response-type probabilities in a no-selection randomized experiment under \(W\perp Z\mid U\), treatment exogeneity, invertible cell matrices, and determinant-ratio separation. The experimental overlap theorem proves agreement after the label conversion \((00,01,10,11)=(4,2,3,1)\); the explicit selected assignment-boundary datum is a separate coverage check outside those experimental conditions. Kawakami (2021), Figure 2(b), equation (2), Theorem 1(i)--(iii) on page 12134, and the proof on pages 12135--12137 give the closer no-selection IV-plus-proxy comparison: the theorem assumes the recursive factorization, invertibility of \(A_{11,x}\), \(A_{22,x}\), \(A_x\), \(Q_{1,x}\), and \(P_{1,x}-Q_{1,x}\), cross-treatment separation of the second columns of the two displayed block ratios, and the exclusions \(Y_{x,z,w}=Y_x\) and \(X_{z,w}=X_z\); it identifies all four joint potential-outcome-type probabilities, with treatment-conditional weights recovered in the appendix for PN and PS. The supporting scope theorem records target agreement on the overlap and exhibits one selected boundary datum for which \(A_x\) is singular but the response-cycle atlas is rigid. This is an overlap and scope-separation comparison only; neither result is asserted to subsume or extend the other. Shu, Wang, and Li (2025, arXiv:2505.15274), Theorems 2--7, develop representative discrete PoC queries, equivalence and replaceability, and sound closed-form bounds from standard experimental and observational distributions; the current version reports low-dimensional computational tightness and leaves general-dimensional tightness open. That compatible-model characterization omits selected proxy-factorization restrictions and does not supply a labeled response-cycle target-constancy atlas. Its feasible region is a response-function polytope cut out by standard margins, whereas the present selected proxy-cycle fiber is generally nonpolyhedral and is cut out by proxy factorizations, supplied or induced margins, and selection restrictions; no inclusion relation is asserted. Miao, Geng, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2018), formula (5), establishes that a causal functional can be identified without identifying its proxy mechanism, but treats an average effect under a linear proxy operator. Krone and Kubjas (2021), Proposition 3.3, supplies admissible-motion cones and separates infinitesimal, local, and global NMF rigidity. Gillis and Rajk\'o (2023), Theorems 5--9, provides partial factor-identifiability and sequential recovery tools, while PN/PS can be rigid without recovery of the relevant columns. Wang and Yuan (2026), Theorem 1 and its matrix specialization, gives sufficient support-scattering uniqueness conditions rather than an if-and-only-if causal target criterion. Zhang et al. (2023), Theorem 3.4, informs regular inference under nuisance nonuniqueness. Andrews and Mikusheva (2016) informs weak-identification calibration, and Turner and Grünwald (2022) supplies exact contingency-table inversion; here a Berger--Boos calibrated profile deviance is inverted through the changing legal SCM correspondence. Tian and Pearl (2000) supplies the published PN/PS benchmark used only as a validation corollary on the no-selection, treatment-exogenous, monotone submodel.
technical_internal_limitation: The all-rank-two two-proxy branch and the residual-ratio reduction have strong presolve support, but the complete mixed-support gluing theorem is unproved. Generic fixed-dimensional real-algebraic decision procedures establish decidability only; reporting a two-copy quantifier-elimination test would not satisfy the proposed structural-classification contribution. For arbitrary real observables, exactness is relative to the ordered coefficient field and carries no bit-complexity claim. Integer-polynomial certificates, rational isolating intervals, and bit bounds apply only to explicitly rational inputs. The Kawakami comparison is limited to agreement on its no-selection regular conditions and one explicit selected boundary law violating its Theorem 1(i) invertibility condition; no subsumption or extension is claimed. No claim is made that every rigid target is rational, that every boundary ambiguity has strictly positive twins, or that confidence sets shrink at genuinely unidentified collision laws.
honest_scope: The central open content is Open-ended Question 1, and the proposal is field-tier. The proposed theorem permits coefficient-field algebraic outputs and requires strict-positive twins only for interior nonrigid strata. Integer-polynomial certificates and bit bounds require explicitly encoded rational observables. Population-margin positivity is not maintained independently: every compatible law with positive selected cells and \(c=P(S=1)>0\) satisfies it, while design-A margins remain supplied observables. The chart evaluator, estimator, covariance output, and reported region are total; absence of a certified separated rigid chart triggers the declared numerical and full-square fallbacks. Covariance consistency and Wald coverage are asserted only for first-order-compatible charts separated from incompatible chart closures, with twice continuously differentiable extensions, proportional margin sampling when needed, and target covariance bounded away from singularity. Confidence-fiber inversion provides honest coverage at every transition; first-order Hausdorff agreement with Wald is asserted only on separated regular strata, and no shrinking-diameter assertion is made at genuinely unidentified laws. The Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki and Shingaki--Kuroki statements are supporting overlap-agreement and boundary-coverage checks, not comparative extension claims. Kawakami's no-selection IV-plus-proxy result is compared through its Figure 2(b), equation (2), and Theorem 1(i)--(iii): agreement is claimed only on the common regular scope, and the explicit selected boundary datum supplies only a strict scope separation through failure of \(A_x\) invertibility. Neither theorem is claimed to subsume or extend the other. The Shu--Wang--Li compatible-model polytope and the selected proxy-cycle fiber encode different information, so no subsumption claim is made. Known-selection reweighting is an implementation normalization, and the Tian--Pearl reduction is a published validation sanity check under the local hypotheses \(S=1\) almost surely, \(X\perp U\), and \(P(U=3)=0\); neither is part of the claimed research-result slate. The GEUVADIS analysis certifies consequences conditional on the stated proxy, exclusion, selection, and IV assumptions; population labels and genotype variables do not empirically prove those assumptions.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The nonunique bridge identification argument, solution-set estimator, influence function theorem, and Discussion were read.
seed_details.proof_boundary: A linear causal functional can annihilate the null space of a bridge operator even when the bridge is nonunique. The proxy-cycle analogue is nonlinear and face-dependent.
